blocks.text: Winchelsea — 3738 Norfolk Street and 3733 Norfolk Street

The sub-area's one verified apartment-condo complex, by Adera per current listings ("WINCHELSEA by Adera"), filed expressly under Central BN in the listing feeds. Listings at 3738 Norfolk Street record the building as built in 1993, freehold strata, with in-suite laundry, 2 secure side-by-side underground parking stalls and 1 storage locker for the unit checked, strata inclusions listing gas and hot water, and pets recorded as allowed ("Pets, Yes" in one listing's fields; "Pet friendly building" in another). A building directory records the companion address, 3733 Norfolk Street, as Winchelsea built in 1994, offering elevator, in-suite laundry, storage and wheelchair access. The 1993 vs 1994 year difference between the two addresses is noted, not resolved — the two addresses may be phases of one complex; unit count and the strata's published rental/age restrictions are not confirmed from the sources checked. School catchments named in the listings are Cascade Heights Elementary and Moscrop Secondary.

items.t: Central is the civic heart of Burnaby along Canada Way, around Burnaby City Hall, Burnaby Central Secondary and the west shore of Deer Lake. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; the area is centred on Canada Way between Willingdon Avenue and Deer Lake — exact MLS boundary streets: Not verified. City of Burnaby use of "Central" as an official neighbourhood name was not confirmed on a City source.

Where the condo stock concentrates: it barely does. The only verified apartment-condo complex is a small 1990s low-rise on Norfolk Street in the Cascade Heights pocket; the rest of the verified attached stock is townhouses on Norfolk and Smith.

Main streets: Canada Way is the main road through the area, with Willingdon Avenue to the west and Sperling Avenue to the east; Highway 1 runs to the north. Norfolk Street and Smith Avenue carry the verified attached stock in the Cascade Heights pocket.

Transit anchors: there is no SkyTrain station inside the Central sub-area; Metrotown Station (Expo Line) is south-west and Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) is north-east of the area. The sourced transit offer is Canada Way bus service between those stations — do not market a Central condo as station-adjacent.

items.t: "Central" is the GVR board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby: Burnaby's civic heart along Canada Way between Willingdon Avenue and Deer Lake, around City Hall and Burnaby Central Secondary. Street-by-street boundaries for the MLS sub-area are not verified — no City or board source read publishes them.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the Norfolk Street / Smith Avenue pocket east of Canada Way, facing and near Broadview Park — all four counted complexes sit in that pocket.

Transit: no SkyTrain station sits inside the sub-area; the nearest stations are Metrotown to the south-west and Sperling–Burnaby Lake to the north-east, with Canada Way bus service through the corridor.

Burnaby's own tax office sits in this corridor: the City directs mailed tax payments to Revenue Services at 4949 Canada Way — the same street that gives the sub-area its civic character (City Hall is at 4949 Canada Way).

Parkside Greene's marketing point is literal: the complex sits at the end of a cul-de-sac a few feet from Broadview Park and its trails, per its listings — the park frontage is why the complex carries "Parkside" in its name.

Norfolk Street carries three of the sub-area's four townhouse complexes plus its only apartment building (Winchelsea) within a few blocks — Norfolk Terrace (4025), Smith + Norfolk (3868), Parkside Greene (3888) and Winchelsea (3738/3733) — a small attached-housing street inside an otherwise detached, civic corridor.

Established side-street lots: detached single-family houses on the Canada Way side streets, with civic and institutional land around City Hall and Deer Lake and a small number of apartment buildings along Canada Way and toward Metrotown. (SnapStats, September 2026)

Lot character, only: typical Central lot sizes are not verified at sub-area level — no official source read states them. The only sourced lot figures are the R1 SSMUH thresholds: a minimum lot area of 281 m² and a minimum lot width of 10 m, with the 280 m² / 281 m² unit-count thresholds in. These are zoning thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Servicing, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable, and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Parcel-level servicing for a specific lot: confirm with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR split is documented for this sub-area, and no ALR percentage is stated. Parcel-level ALR status is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder.
Hazard position: Deer Lake and Deer Lake Brook drain the area's east side; parcel-level streamside setbacks and hazard status are property-specific checks and are not verified for individual lots.

items.t: Nearby areas: Deer Lake and Deer Lake Place to the east, the Burnaby Hospital area and Garden Village to the south, the Vancouver Heights / Capitol Hill side to the north, and Metrotown to the south-west. Central Park is a separate sub-area west of this one — not to be confused with "Central."

Roads and transit: Canada Way is the main road through the area, with Willingdon Avenue to the west and Sperling Avenue to the east; Highway 1 runs to the north. There is no SkyTrain station inside Central; Metrotown Station (Expo Line) is south-west and Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) is north-east of the area.

Parks, library, health: Deer Lake Park, 5435 Sperling Ave, borders the area to the east, with the lake, trails and the city's cultural facilities in the park precinct, and Burnaby City Hall sits in the Deer Lake civic precinct at the sub-area's east end. The library branch serving this area is the Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch, 6100 Willingdon Ave, south-west of the sub-area. The city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Central

items.t: Strata block (for completeness — no Central bare-land strata is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Central ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).
Price land here off a longer window and wider central-Burnaby comparables. (SnapStats, September 2026)

The civic precinct is the east end, not a neighbour: Burnaby City Hall and the Deer Lake cultural precinct sit inside this sub-area's east end — a buyer pricing a side-street lot as purely residential is missing that a large share of the sub-area's land is institutional by design.
